title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
shortDescription: The PCM has detected an electrical fault on the intake air heater control circuit that affects sensor or actuator operation.
fullDescription: This DTC sets when the powertrain control module identifies that the circuit referenced by P0640 has reported voltage outside the calibrated thresholds. Many engine sensors share a common 5V reference voltage from the PCM; a short, open, or shorted sensor on that bus can pull the reference down or up and cause multiple sensor codes to set simultaneously. Diagnosis requires isolating the offending sensor or wiring branch with a methodical disconnect-and-test approach.
safetyImpact: Multiple sensors may report incorrect data, leading to driveability issues, limp mode, or stalling. Address promptly to avoid being stranded.

causes.cause: Short to ground or power on the 5V reference circuit
Failed sensor pulling the reference voltage out of range
Damaged wiring harness, chafed insulation, or corroded connector
Internal PCM reference driver failure
Poor ground connection at PCM or engine block

symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Multiple unrelated sensor DTCs set simultaneously
Engine may enter limp mode or run rough
Erratic gauge readings on the instrument cluster
Hard starting or no-start condition in severe cases

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Pull DTCs from every module, not just the PCM. Reference voltage faults often correlate with several sensor performance codes that point to the offending bus.

fixSteps.title: Measure Reference Voltage at PCM
fixSteps.instruction: With the key on and engine off, backprobe the suspect reference pin at the PCM connector. It should read 4.9-5.1V steady. A low or high reading confirms the bus fault.

fixSteps.title: Isolate the Branch
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect each sensor sharing the reference, one at a time. If voltage returns to spec when a particular sensor is unplugged, that sensor is internally shorted.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully examine the harness branch for chafing against brackets, melting near exhaust components, rodent damage, or moisture in connectors. Repair with solder and adhesive-lined heat shrink.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Sensor or Repair PCM Pin
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the offending sensor with an OEM-grade part. If all sensors test good but the PCM pin is shorted internally, the PCM may need repair or replacement and re-flashing.

faq.q: What does P0640 mean in plain English?
faq.a: It means the PCM saw a wiring or sensor problem on the intake air heater control circuit circuit. Often a single bad sensor pulls the shared 5V supply out of range, triggering this and other related codes.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: If the engine runs normally, short trips are generally OK. But because the fault can affect fueling and emissions, drive only as far as needed to reach a shop.

faq.q: Will replacing the PCM fix it?
faq.a: Rarely. Most reference-voltage faults are caused by a shorted sensor or damaged wiring. Replace the PCM only after confirming every external component on the affected bus is good.
